solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Quickly shift unruly kids, possibly by end of term

parts.note: a chaotic room of unruly children is often called a zoo

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, here of term

explanation.surface: A teacher hurries a rowdy class out of the room, perhaps when the term finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: To zoom is to move very fast, so it fits a quick shift as a verb.

clue.text: 10 — time to interrupt teacher?

indicators.note: one piece breaking into the middle of another is placed inside it

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir

explanation.surface: Is it time to cut in while the teacher is talking?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 10, CAN, in its slang sense of prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang words for prison or jail, so the cross-reference works as a synonym.

clue.text: Dope belonging to half of class

parts.note: something belonging to a group is in it

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word is its first two letters

parts.note: a school class is a form

explanation.surface: A drug discovered on half the pupils in a class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' looks like drugs but means information.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for inside information, the same as the short informal word for facts.

clue.text: Bird entering door to landing

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across these words, as if entering them

explanation.surface: A bird comes in through the door leading to the landing.
explanation.definitionFit: The ortolan is a small European bunting, once eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: Fighting men introduced to part of para's training?

indicators.note: the soldiers are put into the middle of the other piece

parts.note: paratroopers practise freefall, dropping before the parachute opens
OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword abbreviation for soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers are brought in to take part in paratrooper training.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl in which everyone joins in is fighting of the most disorderly kind; the noun stands for a general fight.

clue.text: Hold gift given by sourpuss around middle of Easter

indicators.note: the gift wraps round the centre letters of the festival

parts.note: a boon is a blessing or gift

indicators.note: the two central letters of the six-letter word

parts.note: a crab, or crabby person, is a grumpy sourpuss

explanation.surface: A grump hands over a present in the middle of the Easter holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: A Boston crab is a wrestling hold, the opponent's legs bent back over their body.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a named wrestling grip, so the noun hold covers it as an example.

clue.text: Carpet bombing's beginning — load deployed in space

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter
the shuffled letters go inside the word for space

parts.note: room means space, as in room to move

indicators.note: troops deployed are spread out and rearranged, so the letters of load are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bombing raid begins and a payload is dropped over an open area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' is the anagram signal; 'Carpet bombing' reads as one phrase but the definition is just the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadloom is carpet woven on a wide loom, so it is a kind of carpet.

clue.text: Randomly look at small core of labour force?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: the three central letters of the two words together form the core

explanation.surface: A question about the small heart of the workforce.
explanation.definitionFit: To surf channels or the web is to browse at random, flitting from one thing to the next.

clue.text: Having put on tie, shift grip

parts.note: to put on a spell is to work one; here the phrase stands for spell
to tie is to bind

explanation.surface: Someone dons a necktie and then adjusts their grasp.
explanation.definitionFit: To grip an audience is to hold their attention completely, which is to enthral them.

clue.text: Traveller rings round half the force after stuff is returned

indicators.note: the second piece follows the first
returned means the word is sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: to stuff is to cram

indicators.note: the two circles go round the shortened word

parts.note: two O shapes look like rings

indicators.note: the first three letters make half of the six-letter word

parts.note: the force is a nickname for the police

explanation.surface: An explorer surrounds a police unit once some material has been sent back.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian merchant famous for his journeys to China is a celebrated traveller.

clue.text: First signs of cheap and nasty sack from abroad

indicators.note: the first letters of the next three words are taken

explanation.surface: A cheap, nasty bag imported from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from abroad' marks the American sense: to can someone is to fire them.
explanation.definitionFit: In US slang to can a worker is to dismiss them, the same as British sack.

clue.text: Boss who controls one's will? Not half

indicators.note: only half the word is kept, its first four letters, the rest dropped

parts.note: an executor carries out the terms of a will

explanation.surface: Is the boss the one who decides what you do? Absolutely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is British slang for 'very much', but here it cuts a word in two.
explanation.definitionFit: An executive is a senior manager, and the clipped form is informal for a boss.

clue.text: The whole line cut into ductile metal

indicators.note: the line is cut into the metal symbol, going inside it

parts.note: aluminium, chemical symbol Al, is a metal easily drawn into wire

explanation.surface: A whole line is etched into soft metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Everything together is the entirety; the pronoun means every part of something.

clue.text: Trace place in digs where bill can be left?

parts.note: a trace of something is a sign of it
board is lodging, as in room and board; digs is British slang for rented rooms

explanation.surface: Searching for a spot in one's lodgings to leave the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: The bill is a poster, not an invoice: bills are stuck on boards.
explanation.definitionFit: A board for notices is where a poster or bill is put up, a playful description.

clue.text: Extremely selfish and silly, getting up to worry over mischief

indicators.note: the extreme letters of selfish are its first and last
in a down clue going up reads the word from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: inane means silly

indicators.note: over signals a turn, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to nag is to worry at someone

explanation.surface: A selfish and silly person rises up to fret about mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' turns INANE into ENANI and 'over' turns NAG into GAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Shenanigans are tricks or high jinks, so the singular stands for mischief.

clue.text: Weighty cart, having been jacked up, remains here

parts.note: a weighty matter is a grave one

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting the word up reverses it

parts.note: a dray is a heavy cart, as used by brewers

explanation.surface: A heavy cart, once raised on a jack, stays where it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains' is a noun, a body, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A cemetery is the place where human remains lie buried.

clue.text: Minding one's business?

parts.note: minding means guarding; this person's business is protecting someone

explanation.surface: Keeping one's nose out of other people's affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A protector's job is minding a client, so minding is their business.

clue.text: King of sorts, Elvis regularly needs no backing

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter, here the second and fourth
backing means the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Elvis, the King, every so often needs no support band.
explanation.walkthrough: Elvis was the King of rock and roll, a nice misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: The lion is the king of beasts, so it is a monarch of a kind.

clue.text: Rave organised preceding new announcement about gallery

indicators.note: the shuffled piece comes before the rest
the letters are arranged into a new order
about signals a turn, so the short word is read backwards

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a public announcement

explanation.surface: A dance party is set up ahead of a fresh gallery announcement.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallery can be a roofed open porch along a house, the same structure as a porch or stoop.

clue.text: Leave one in grey cutting grass

indicators.note: the inner piece cuts into the grass word, sitting inside it

parts.note: hay is dried grass

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the word for grey

parts.note: grey-haired people are old
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Leave one inside, grey, mowing the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave from work is time off, a break or vacation.

clue.text: Falters in, say, withdrawn spot

indicators.note: the word for falters goes inside the reversed abbreviation
something withdrawn is pulled back, so read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, is said before an example
to falter in walking is to limp

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles in, perhaps, at a quiet secluded place.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch sight of something briefly is to spot it; both verbs mean to see quickly.

clue.text: Artist leaving flask where 23 10 22

indicators.note: the artist leaves, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: a carafe is a flask or jug for water or wine
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual abbreviation for an artist

explanation.surface: An artist abandons a flask in the place indicated.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads the cross-references: YOU CAN EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A small restaurant serving snacks is a place where diners can eat.

clue.text: Victor may get one girl to accept experienced master

indicators.note: the girl takes in the other letters, which go inside

parts.note: gal is informal for girl
an old hand is experienced
MEd is a Master of Education degree

explanation.surface: A girl agrees to take on a seasoned schoolmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The winner of an Olympic event receives the top prize, a first-place award.

clue.text: Prime bits of hearty feed

indicators.note: the letters in prime-numbered positions, second, third and fifth, are kept and the others go

explanation.surface: The best parts of a substantial meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime' is the number sense: letters 2, 3 and 5 of 'hearty' are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: To feed is to take food, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Eulogy intermittently put about by solver?

indicators.note: the picked letters are turned about and read backwards
every other letter is taken, the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A tribute spread around now and then by a crossword solver.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter addresses the solver as the second person, so the pronoun stands for the solver.

clue.text: Singer eager to make a comeback

indicators.note: coming back is going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: avid means eager

explanation.surface: A performer keen to return to the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female opera singer, a prima donna.

clue.text: Fire is prevented by this spray penetrating most of dry cable's sheath

indicators.note: the spray goes inside the shortened word for dry
most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: arid means dry
mist is a fine spray

indicators.note: a sheath is the outside cover, so the outer letters are taken

explanation.surface: A sprinkler spray cuts into a cable's dry casing, so a fire is stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' means gunfire: a truce stops the shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce between warring sides is a ceasefire, stopping the guns firing.

clue.text: About to stop whole film?

indicators.note: the letter stops up the word, going inside it like a plug

parts.note: the sum is the whole amount
C, circa, means about

explanation.surface: Is someone about to halt an entire movie?
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' is a thin surface layer, not a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Scum is a layer of dirt on top of a liquid, a kind of surface coating.

clue.text: Trace letter from abroad

definitions.meaning: a tiny amount, as in not one jot
a letter of the Greek alphabet, the ninth

explanation.surface: Tracking down a letter sent from overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: It means a very small amount, and it is also a Greek character.

clue.text: Black yet brown? Oddly not

indicators.note: the odd-placed letters are not taken, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Is it black, or perhaps brown? Strangely, it is neither.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebon is a poetic word for black, from ebony wood.

clue.text: Note in pad, a spelling aid

indicators.note: the note letter goes inside the word for pad

parts.note: a wad of cotton is a pad

explanation.surface: A memo jotted in a notepad helps with spelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spelling' means casting spells, not writing words correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician's stick helps cast spells, an aid to spelling in the magic sense.

clue.text: Alternatively, pundits or I get upset

indicators.note: read as 'arranged another way', the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Either the commentators or I will lose our temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternatively' looks like a link but signals the rearrangement; 'upset' is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A disturbance or interruption of normal order is a disruption.
